name: Entrypoint Branch/PR Switch (static credentials)
description: Demonstrates pattern B from docs/extensions/lifecycle-hooks.md: {option.ref} wired directly into the entrypoint's own command line, resolved at container-create time - so branch/PR switching works from container start, with no dependency on launch.sh's timing. Accepts a bare branch name, a bare (optionally '#'-prefixed) PR number, or a full GitHub branch/PR URL copied from the browser. See mounts.bind below for how to add a statically-provisioned deploy key for a private repo.

options.name: ref
options.label: Branch or PR #
options.placeholder: e.g. main, a PR number like 42, or a github.com/.../tree|pull/... URL

command:
set -e
apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y -qq git sudo >/dev/null
REPO=/home/dockside/app
REF="$1"
# For a private repo: uncomment the mounts.bind entry above, then add:
#   export GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh -i /home/dockside/.ssh/deploy_key -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new"
# and use a git@... URL below instead of the https:// one.
[ -d "$REPO/.git" ] || git clone https://github.com/newsnowlabs/dockside.git "$REPO"
cd "$REPO"
# See resolve_tree_branch() in app/scripts/container/launch.sh for the full rationale
# (identical logic): the longest-prefix-first search is not just a heuristic - git's
# hierarchical ref namespace means "feature" and "feature/foo" can never both exist as
# branches at once, so there is exactly one real branch any given URL remainder could
# resolve to.
resolve_tree_branch() {
  CANDIDATE="$1"
  while [ -n "$CANDIDATE" ]; do
    if git ls-remote --exit-code origin "refs/heads/$CANDIDATE" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "$CANDIDATE"
      return 0
    fi
    case "$CANDIDATE" in
      */*) CANDIDATE="${CANDIDATE%/*}" ;;
      *) return 1 ;;
    esac
  done
  return 1
}
# A single 'ref' option covers several forms: a bare branch name; a bare PR number
# (optionally '#'-prefixed); or a full GitHub URL copied from the browser - see
# checkout_git_ref() in app/scripts/container/launch.sh, which uses the same logic.
PR="" BRANCH=""
case "$REF" in
  https://github.com/*/pull/*)
    PR=${REF#*/pull/}
    PR=${PR%%[/?#]*}
    ;;
  https://github.com/*/tree/*)
    CANDIDATE=${REF#*/tree/}
    CANDIDATE=${CANDIDATE%%[?#]*}
    BRANCH=$(resolve_tree_branch "$CANDIDATE") || BRANCH="$CANDIDATE"
    ;;
  https://github.com/*/commits/*)
    CANDIDATE=${REF#*/commits/}
    CANDIDATE=${CANDIDATE%%[?#]*}
    BRANCH=$(resolve_tree_branch "$CANDIDATE") || BRANCH="$CANDIDATE"
    ;;
  *)
    NUM="${REF#'#'}"
    case "$NUM" in
      ''|*[!0-9]*) BRANCH="$REF" ;;
      *)           PR="$NUM" ;;
    esac
    ;;
esac
if [ -n "$PR" ]; then
  # Two statements, not "git fetch ... && git checkout ...": under `set -e`, a
  # non-final command in an && list is exempt from aborting the script on
  # failure, so a bad PR number would otherwise fail silently and fall through.
  git fetch origin "refs/pull/$PR/head"
  git checkout FETCH_HEAD
elif [ -n "$BRANCH" ]; then
  git fetch origin "refs/heads/$BRANCH:refs/remotes/origin/$BRANCH"
  git switch "$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null || git switch --track -c "$BRANCH" "origin/$BRANCH"
fi
sleep infinity
